interfacePatterns.title: Architecture from context to components
interfacePatterns.reason: supports inspect, trace; serves understand, inspect; fits hierarchy
apply: Show current and proposed elements distinctly
Name boundary ownership
Label arrows by their exact relationship
Expose contracts and material omissions in the inspector
avoid: One diagram containing every abstraction level
Boxes with no owner or contract meaning

interfacePatterns.title: Completion receipt and next step
interfacePatterns.reason: supports inspect, confirm; serves understand; fits list
apply: State the completed outcome
Give the exact evidence identity
Explain what happens next
Keep limitations adjacent
avoid: Calling a supporting artifact the user outcome
Adding a feedback survey as the default next step

interfacePatterns.title: Linked work and system lenses
interfacePatterns.reason: supports inspect, trace; serves understand; fits hierarchy
apply: Name the question answered by each lens
Keep edge semantics distinct per lens
Carry stable semantic selection across views
Keep one inspector and provenance grammar
avoid: Combining work dependencies and system interfaces in one graph
Calling a work graph an architecture diagram
Changing the selected subject silently when switching lenses

interfacePatterns.title: Review before completion
interfacePatterns.reason: supports inspect, confirm; serves inspect; fits list
apply: Show what changed
Bind evidence to the exact revision
Separate pass evidence from limitations
Offer approve and request-changes dispositions
avoid: Equating green tests with human acceptance
Making the reviewer reconstruct the change from raw files

interfacePatterns.title: Task list with meaningful progress

compositionPlan.coldReadTarget: After a minute a newcomer can say what the page answers: A visitor types one sentence goal; a model drafts outcome -> 3-5 success criteria (each with a disproof sentence) -> 1-2 evidence requirements (kind: deterministic test, runtime observation, human review) -> how each would be proven; AES validation accepts it or refuses it with named violations, and every accepted criterion shows INSUFFICIENT because nothing is proven yet. A one-click hand-written refused proposal shows the refusal case.
sketchInstructions: Put one short title at the top that states what this page answers and for whom.
Everything important is visible at once; no scrolling implied.
One main drawing occupies most of the area; other elements are visibly smaller and lighter.
Use at most three type sizes; headings heavier than body; important boxes larger.
Entry point top-left; the thing to do next bottom-right; if the order differs, number the parts.
Related items touch or nearly touch; unrelated items have clear gaps between them.
Every object of one kind is drawn the same way in every picture of the set.
Draw at most one level of boxes-around-groups; use white space for the rest.
Left edges of text and boxes line up on a few shared vertical lines.
Reuse one card style, one label style, and one legend position across the set.
Leave generous empty space around the main drawing and between groups.
No decorative borders, shadows, icons, or gridlines that carry no meaning.
Draw context in light grey and the subject in black.
Show the variants as a grid of identical small panels on one scale.
The first view is the whole; a detail panel shows what opens when something is selected.
Exactly one kind of thing is highlighted; everything else is grey scale.
Draw each part in the form that fits its job: list, table, flow, or map.
Connections are lines or containment, not just items placed near each other.
One large drawing with a few short labels pointing at parts of it; no columns of text.
Only draw a section or tab if the content shown needs it.
If things change over time, include a small time strip on the same screen.
A stranger should get the point from the title and the main drawing alone.
Show a handful of objects at readable size, not dozens at tiny size.
